title: Prospective UREthral Stricture Treatment Registry
summary:
Background

A narrowing of the urethra can cause difficulties with urination and may significantly affect quality of life. Different treatment options are available, including minimally invasive procedures performed through the urethra and open surgical operations. It is not yet fully clear which treatment provides the best long-term results.

Research Question

This study examines how safe and effective the different treatment approaches are and how they affect symptoms, quality of life, and patient satisfaction.

Methodology

Patients who undergo treatment for a narrowing of the urethra will be followed over a longer period of time. Information will be collected on the course of treatment, possible complications, any additional procedures, and patient-reported symptoms and quality of life. The treatment itself is not influenced by participation in the study and is carried out according to standard medical practice.

interventions.name:
Endoscopic or open surgical treatment of anterior urethral stricture or posterior urethral stenosis, including bladder neck stenosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged 18 years or older who are capable of giving informed consent and undergoing endoscopic or open surgical treatment of a urethral stricture or stenosis.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who are not capable of giving informed consent and individuals under 18 years of age.
